terms.grammar: verb, defective: perfect in form, present in meaning
terms.comment: Ōdī, I hate; ōderam, I hated; ōderō, I shall hate. With an infinitive too (Hor. Ep. 1.16.52, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: turn up one’s nose at, loathe (food above all)
terms.comment: The fussy eater’s verb: Lewis & Short, “to shrink or flinch from any thing unpleasant to the taste”. Not frequent before Augustus.
With ab: a milder way to say “I hate”.

phrases.latin: ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris.
phrases.english: I hate and I love. Why do I do it, you may ask.

phrases.latin: ōdimus accipitrem, quia vīvit semper in armīs
phrases.english: we hate the hawk, because it lives always armed

phrases.latin: Omnīnō ōdī surgere tam bene māne.
phrases.english: I absolutely hate getting up so early.
